title: ArtibotMissionContract
description: In-memory validator contract for the output of the intent.md parser. This schema is NOT a disk artifact and no file is ever written in this shape: `.artibot/missions/<mission_id>/intent.md` is the canonical on-disk form, and this schema validates the object a parser produces from it (design v1 3.1, 'mission-contract.schema.yaml 은 파서 출력의 메모리 내 검증기'). Derived-file generation is forbidden, so a consumer that persists an instance of this schema is violating the design. Extends the v1.0 13-field contract (package/03_INTENT_MISSION_COMPILER.md) with the reverse additions mission_id, intent_revision, status, topology, review and user_decisions, plus execution_profile and schema_version.

schema_version.description: Common-meta field. Shape kept byte-identical to `common-meta.schema.json#/$defs/schema_version` (T-19), which is the authority: a monotonic INTEGER version of the artifact schema, not a semver string and not the instance's `revision`. Inlined rather than $ref'd because draft-07 drops keywords sitting beside a $ref and because this schema must stay loadable on its own. Reserved only in Phase 0 — deliberately NOT in `required`; enforcement across artifacts is a P2 decision.

mission_id.description: Reverse addition from intent.md frontmatter. Two accepted forms: the issued mission id `M-<YYYYMMDD>-<NNN>`, where NNN may run PAST three digits so a busy day cannot overflow the id space (04_INTENT_MD_SPEC.md:27), and the session fallback `M-<YYYYMMDD>-S<sid8>` used for non-substantive interactions so ledger envelopes keep their required field (design 3.1, PRD R-09). The pattern is kept BYTE-IDENTICAL to schemas/ledger-envelope.schema.json and schemas/review-output.schema.json: a mission_id valid in a contract must be valid in the ledger and in a review, or the join across those three breaks. Do not tighten it here alone. Issuance is two-stage and parent-session-only (T-24); /split workers inherit rather than issue.

intent_revision.description: Reverse addition from intent.md frontmatter. Monotonic revision of the interpreted intent. Substantive signal S6 keys off a follow-up to an existing mission's intent_revision, and review binding (assertIntentBinding) re-checks this value at completion time.

status.description: Reverse addition. The canonical 7-state mission vocabulary from package-v1.1/16_STATE_SCHEMA.yaml. The StateStore task graph is the source of truth; state.yaml and the ops/vNext state sets are projections of it (design 3.5).

goal.description: The interpreted mission goal — what must be achieved and why. Not a transcript of the raw request; the raw text lives in intent.md `## Original Request`.

explicit_requests.description: Protected list of what the user literally asked for (Intent Fidelity Rule). Upgraded from v1.0 `array of string` to objects carrying a `span` back into the original request, so a systemic finding cannot silently substitute a different target for the user's words. Widening scope needs only a plan revision; narrowing or replacing an entry here requires an evidence-backed intent revision (design 3.1).

span.description: Character offsets of this request inside the preserved original request text. The span is what binds the frontmatter array item back to the user's words; without it the anti-substitution check has nothing to compare against.

inferred_outcomes.description: Outcomes the interpreter inferred but the user did not state. Never promoted into explicit_requests.

success.description: Success criteria in four sub-sections, mirroring intent.md `## Success Criteria`.

scope.description: Problem boundary. `requested_target` is what the user pointed at; the other lists are the 5-way classification the boundary pass produces. Scope may widen only with a causal justification.

requested_target.description: Fail-closed: at least one target. A contract whose requested_target is empty has lost the thing the user pointed at, which is exactly the context-substitution failure the constitution forbids (design 3.1 first eval case).

constraints.description: Explicit limits on how the mission may be carried out.

findings.description: Blindspot classes. `bounded_blindspots` may be fixed autonomously; `future_opportunities` are recorded and must not silently become a large refactor.

human_gates.description: HUMAN_GATE_MATRIX identifiers (HG-01 through HG-13) this mission expects to hit. Enforcement lives in the PreToolUse hook, not here.

intent_confidence.description: Uncertainty represented rather than hidden. Low confidence triggers investigation first, not a user question. Axis set copied verbatim from package/03_INTENT_MISSION_COMPILER.md; `product_decision_required` is substantive signal S4.

command_activation.description: NOT a first-class field. Hardening 2 overrode the lane-1 contract: natural language compiles to an execution profile, and command_activation is only a DERIVED PROJECTION of that profile, kept so the Shadow metric 'activation vs actual slash command' stays measurable. Never treat it as an input, and never round-trip a profile through it — `execution_profile` is the authority.

execution_profile.description: The 8-key execution profile (reasoning, autonomy, performance, parallelism, planning, context, review, completion), owned by T-18. Referenced by the `$id` that `execution-profile.schema.json` declares for itself, not by relative path, so resolution does not depend on where either file sits on disk. A validator that has not been given the target schema cannot check this subtree at all — treat the absence of errors there as 'not checked', never as 'well-formed'.

topology.description: Reverse addition. `mode` uses the run-ledger 6-value enum, which design 3.5 makes the canonical router-output vocabulary. v1.1 06_STATE_YAML_SPEC.md also put `performance_profile` here; decision F2 moved that dimension to execution_profile.performance, so it is deliberately absent.

review.description: Reverse addition, mirroring state.yaml `review{required,model,status}`. The verdict vocabulary itself belongs to review-output v2 and its adapter map (T-20); `status` is intentionally an unconstrained string here so this schema does not fork that vocabulary.

user_decisions.description: Reverse addition. Decisions the user actually made (AskUserQuestion answers), carried so a later agent cannot re-litigate them. Shape left open, matching package/schemas/adr.schema.yaml which declares `user_decisions: {type: array}` with no item constraint.
